_comment: Edit this file, not the code. Bands: 1 cheap workhorse, 2 mid, 3 deep. Ladders are ordered preferences; the router filters by live quota and then prefers the eligible candidate whose quota bucket resets soonest (spend what expires first).

claude._note: Claude Code publishes no quota API. Leave null and Claude stays escalation-only (band 3). Set a token budget to let it take ordinary work.

openrouter._note: 1000/day applies with 10 USD or more of lifetime credit, otherwise 50/day. Counted locally in state.json.

_comment_free: opencode_zen entries here are the -free models, served to the OpenCode client without touching the Go subscription buckets. Slower than the paid cheap band, so the ladder keeps them last: overflow capacity, not the default.
_comment_cache: Seconds a quota reading stays usable for routing. A dispatch takes minutes, so a reading a minute old is the same reading. `rightsize probe` and `route --fresh` always re-read.

launchers._doc: How a decision becomes a command. Each launcher maps a provider to a template, with `default` covering the rest. Fields: {provider} {agent} {model} {model_ref} {effort} {band} {spec} {spec_path}. Adding a launcher is config, not code: see docs/ADAPTERS.md.

orca._doc: A worker-start launches a worker, which is by definition not the coordinator, so it gets its own worktree. `--worktree current` reuses the main checkout: the worker shares the coordinator's tree and branch, can write to main mid-merge, and cleanup can never find it because there is no worktree to remove. One such worker ran in a main checkout for 29 hours. For opencode the model is bound by creating the terminal with `opencode -m <model>` and attaching the worker to it, because `--agent opencode` takes no model flag and `OPENCODE_MODEL` is ignored: a worker launched without the binding silently runs the default in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, and `rightsize audit` exists to catch exactly that. Verified 2026-09-20 end to end. Use orca-current only when sharing the checkout is the point.
orca.default:
# once per coordinator terminal, if `orca orchestration run-current` shows none:
#   orca orchestration run-create --objective "<what this batch is for>" --json
orca worktree create --name {name} --json > /dev/null
HANDLE=$(orca terminal create --worktree name:{name} --command 'opencode -m {model_ref}' --json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["terminal"]["handle"])')
orca orchestration worker-start --spec {spec} --worktree name:{name} --terminal "$HANDLE" --json

orca-current._doc: Deliberately shares the coordinator's checkout. For a supervised leg you are watching, a quick review, or a task that must see uncommitted work in the current tree. Never for unsupervised work.
orca-current.default:
orca orchestration worker-start --spec {spec} --worktree current --agent {agent} --json
# then inside that terminal: opencode -m {model_ref}

_comment_dispatch_cost: Percentage points one dispatch is expected to burn, multiplied by the band. A coarse estimate on purpose: the exact number is unknowable before the worker runs, and being roughly right is what stops a fan-out from overcommitting a plan. Raise it if a batch of workers routinely takes a provider past its reserve.
_comment_max_inflight: How many dispatches may be in flight on one provider at once. This is the spread lever for a large fan-out: when a provider is full the next task goes to the next eligible one instead of queueing behind it.
_comment_reservation: How long a reservation holds capacity when nobody reports the dispatch done. A worker that dies silently must not hold a plan hostage, so this expires on its own; `rightsize report <provider> --done` releases it immediately.

effort._comment: Reasoning effort per band, for the CLIs that take the knob. The band picks the model; effort is the second dial on that model. A wide blast radius, an irreversible step, or a retry after a failed attempt each raise it one level. Providers absent here get no effort flag at all. Levels: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.

_comment_openrouter: OpenRouter is probed but deliberately not on a worker ladder. Verified 2026-09-20: its free models answer a direct API call, but dispatching one through the opencode CLI fails with 413 Request too large, because an agent sends a system prompt and tool definitions that the free endpoint will not accept. Put it back on a ladder once either a paid model is laddered (the key here carries its own 0.01 USD spend limit, so raise that first at openrouter.ai/settings/keys) or a launcher exists that dispatches with a small payload.
_comment_staleness: How old a file-sourced reading may be before it is treated as unknown rather than current. Only Codex needs this: its numbers are written when Codex runs, so between sessions the reading ages while the real quota moves. An old HIGH reading is the dangerous direction, because it blocks a provider that may have reset hours ago, and unknown already means escalation-only rather than unusable. Verified 2026-09-20: `codex exec` does not write a rollout, so only an interactive Codex session refreshes this.
